{{Quote|Halt! You are trespassing on Naescorcom property. You are under arrest!|Lieutenant Mish Paht, to the freelance agents that he accosted on S-Ipsus|<ref name="OA" />}}
[[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] '''Mish Paht''' was a [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] who served in the [[Thaereian military]] during the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Around [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], Paht led a group of [[Thaereian]] [[Soldier/Legends|troops]] to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Genarius]] to recover evidence of a [[Anti-Caarite virus|virus]] [[Death/Legends|fatal]] to the [[Caarite]] [[Species/Legends|species]] that had been developed by the [[Believers]] [[Sith cult/Legends|Sith cult]]. In the Genarius [[Factory/Legends|manufacturing facility]] [[S-Ipsus]], Paht and his soldiers accosted a group of [[Heroes of Cularin|freelance agents]] that had recovered a specimen of the contagion in an attempt to claim the viral sample for the Thaereian military. However, he was defeated by the freelance operatives and was unsuccessful at appropriating the specimen.

==Biography==
{{Quote|We're the duly appointed protectors of Cularin. You need to give us any evidence you have about anything bad. You know. Anything&hellip;bad. I can't tell you specifically, that would compromise the safety of the system.|Lieutenant Mish Paht, to the freelance agents that he accosted on S-Ipsus|<ref name="OA" />}}
Mish Paht was a [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Bothan/Legends|Bothan]] who served as a [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] in the [[Thaereian military]],<ref name="OA" /> the armed forces of the [[Thaereian system]],<ref name="OT">{{Wizards|url=rpga/livingforce/article.asp?x=lf/swlf20011004b_thaere&c=swlfc|text=Over Thaere}}</ref> during the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="OA" /> Around 21 BBY,<ref name="date">The ''[[Living Force Campaign Guide]]'' states that the [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|Living Force]] campaign is set one [[Standard year/Legends|year]] after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], an event that is dated to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. As the ''Living Force'' adventure ''[[Below the Belt: Philology|Philology]]'' [[Cularin's disappearance|moved]] the campaign forward ten years to the time of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the events depicted in ''[[Metatheran Caution: Open Aarms|Open Aarms]]'' can therefore be dated to circa [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]].</ref> a [[S-Ipsus Believers laboratory|concealed laboratory]] employed by the [[Believers]] [[Sith cult/Legends|Sith cult]] to refine a [[Anti-Caarite virus|virus]] [[Death/Legends|fatal]] to the [[Caarite]] [[Species/Legends|species]] was uncovered by the [[Metatheran Cartel]] trading concern on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Genarius]]. Upon learning of the discovery, Paht determined to recover evidence of the Believer operation to advance his standing within the [[Thaereian]] military.<ref name="OA" />

To that end, Paht led a Thaereian patrol to [[S-Ipsus]], a [[Factory/Legends|manufacturing station]] on Genarius upon which the Believer laboratory was sited. Ostensibly, Paht and his troops investigated the virus in accordance with the Thaereian military's [[Thaereian Navy charter|enfranchisement]] by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] as defenders of the [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]]. In truth however, the Thaereians' presence on S-Ipsus was illegal due to the facility being the private property of the [[Naescorcom/Legends|Naescorcom]] conglomerate and hence outside of the Thaereians' jurisdiction, a fact of which Paht was aware. As protection against the virus, Paht donned an [[Environment suit/Legends|EVA suit]] emblazoned with the insignia of the Thaereian military.<ref name="OA" />

{{RPG|''[[Metatheran Caution: Open Aarms|Open Aarms]]''}}
Paht and his [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] entered a [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonator]] production line on S-Ipsus beneath which the Believer laboratory was located. On arrival they crossed paths with a group of [[Heroes of Cularin|freelance agents]] investigating the [[Sith cultist/Legends|cultists']] activities who had recovered an active sample of the virus and captured the Believer [[Canduri]]. Paht accused the freelancers of trespassing on Naescorcom property, planning to use this pretence as a basis to arrest the group in order to gain custody of Canduri. He also claimed that it was not safe for the operatives on S-Ipsus, though refused to disclose what he knew of the Believers activities there. The standoff erupted into a firefight and the freelance agents defeated Paht and his compatriots and escapees with their Believer [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoner]].<ref name="OA" />

Following the attack, the Thaereian military sought to disavow responsibility for Paht's unlawful actions on Genarius. The Bothan [[Officer/Legends|officer]] was accused of firing on innocent civilians on private property and removed from active service to await trial. In a public message published on the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]], the Thaereian military apologized to the people of the Cularin system for Paht's crimes and claimed that he had acted without authority.<ref name="OA" />
{{Endgame}}

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Are you getting lippy with me?|Lieutenant Mish Paht, to the freelance agents that he accosted on S-Ipsus|<ref name="OA" />}}
Mish Paht was an ambitious and believed he would progress far within the Thaereian military. He was corrupt and antagonistic by nature and he was willing to perform acts of violence to advance his career. Paht's arrogance led to him overreaching himself when investigating the Believers' presence on Genarius and he wanted to recover evidence of the anti-Caarite virus at any cost.<ref name="OA" />

==Behind the scenes==
Mish Paht was created by [[Morrie Mullins]] and featured as a non-player character in ''[[Metatheran Caution: Open Aarms|Open Aarms]]'', a [[2003]] [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] module that formed part of the [[Metatheran Caution trilogy]] of [[RPGA]]'s [[Living Force (roleplaying campaign)|Living Force]] campaign.<ref name="OA" />

In the roleplaying adventure, the players roleplay as the freelance agents that Paht encounters on Genarius and his encounter with them can play out in a number of ways. If any of the player characters are equipped with restricted weapons, Paht demands to see a permit. He also offers to allow the agents' possession of any unauthorized weapons to go unpunished if the freelance operatives surrender their arms to him, though it is possible for the player characters to bribe Paht or otherwise convince him into allowing them to keep any illegal weapons. If Paht is told by the player characters that he has no authority on S-Ipsus to arrest them, he desists from attempting to detain the freelance agents but continues to demand that the agents relinquish Canduri and any other evidence the player characters gathered concerning the anti-Caarite virus to the Thaereians.<ref name="OA" />

It is possible for the encounter between Paht and the player characters to be resolved via non-violent means by the freelance agents handing over Canduri or convincing Paht to let them leave unhindered. If the player characters deceive Paht and he realizes they are lying to him, he orders his troops to open fire on the agents and it is then possible for Paht to be defeated or killed. Afterward, if Paht and his troops opened fire on the freelance agents the Bothan officer is reprimanded by the Thaereian military and a public statement is issued by the Thaereians to apologize for his actions.<ref name="OA" />
